incumbent_comparison: Better than rocking_chair-v002: lowering the curved runners reduced the measured floor gap from 0.542 inches to 0.032 inches while retaining the full-depth sweep, slatted back, arms, and validated bounds.

observations.art_direction_fit: The simple warm low-poly hardwood form matches the existing room style and furniture palette.
observations.close_up_quality: The close view resolves the back slats, seat and runners; a separate computer tower from the RoomDefinition remains near the chair but does not erase the silhouette.
observations.gameplay_readability: The chair is legible in the production room; the independent RoomDefinition obstacle and the separate tower remain unchanged.
observations.geometric_detail: The captures show seven back slats, a crest rail, paired posts, arms, tenons, and segmented curved runners with brass pins.
observations.material_realism: Warm hardwood grain and alternating back slats remain visible in production lighting.
observations.proportion: The chair has a plausible traditional profile, and the updated runner position brings its bottom closer to the floor without crowding the seat.
observations.scale_fidelity: The scene measures 20.5 x 37.27 x 27.97 inches and is normalized to the existing 24 x 38 x 31-inch room object; the runner bottom is 0.032 inches above the floor.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The production three-quarter capture clearly shows a wood rocking chair with slatted back, arms, seat, and two curved runners.
observations.silhouette_quality: The revised long runners approach the floor and complete the expected rocker silhouette; the slatted back remains distinct.
observations.surface_variation: The hardwood texture and alternating slat tones provide restrained surface variation consistent with the room.
observations.technical_integration: Godot validates 71 meshes and the corrected bounds; the production resolver loads rocking_chair-v003 for all six standardized captures without fallback.
